predecessors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
predecessors.text: Dahala mandala (Baghelkhand), the Chedi country, with the capital Tripuri near Jabalpur

ledger.x: 850: Kokalla I lays the foundation of the Kalachuri power at Tripuri.

c. 1000: the Ratnapura branch is set up in Chhattisgarh as a Tripuri vassal. "The Ratnapura branch was established by Kalinga-raja around 1000 CE... They were an offshoot of the Kalachuris of Tripuri, and ruled as vassals of the parent dynasty for many years." Kalinga-raja took Dakshina Kosala from the Somavamshis…

ledger.cp: unknown (page silent on who held Prayaga)

ledger.x: c. 1050 (bridge): Lakshmikarna subjugates the Chandela Devavarman. "Lakshmikarna subjugated the Chandela king Devavarman (r. c. 1050-1060 CE)"; the Kalachuris page adds that Devavarman "seems to have died in a battle against him". The page gives no year for the subjugation; 1050 is the start of Devavarman's reign.

c. 1055: Lakshmikarna joins Bhima of Gujarat in the attack that topples the Paramara Bhoja. "Around 1055 CE, he played an important role in the downfall of the Paramara king Bhoja"; he "captured a part of the Paramara kingdom of Malwa after Bhoja's death" but lost it within months when "Jayasimha gained back his…

c. 1073: the Paramara Udayaditya ends the Kalachuri hold on Malwa. The Lakshmikarna page lists losing Malwa to Udayaditya "around 1073 CE" among the signs of decline, with the abdication to Yashahkarna.
1073: the page gives the raid only; no withdrawal date.
before 1075-76: Kirttivarman frees the Chandela kingdom.
1085 (bridge): Varanasi and the north pass to the Gahadavalas.
1123-1135 (bridge): Ratna-deva II of Ratnapura declares independence.

c. 1152 (bridge): the Chandela Madanavarman takes northern Baghelkhand. "lost some of his northern territory to the Chandela king Madanavarman"; the Chandelas "captured the northern part of Baghelkhand". The page gives no year; 1152 is the year the Chandela dossier carries for the same event (Cliopatria's Chandela…

c. 1212: last attested Kalachuri king. Trailokya-malla "ruled at least until 1212 CE"; "It is not known when and how his rule ended"; in the later 13th century the former territories passed to "the Paramaras, Chandelas, the Delhi Sultanate and the Seunas".

wars.name: Paramara raid on Tripuri
wars.outcome: Munja "invaded the Kalachuri kingdom and raided their capital Tripuri" in the reign of Yuvarajadeva II; no land is said to change hands.

wars.name: Gangeyadeva's campaigns
wars.outcome: Gangeyadeva fought the Kalyani Chalukyas, a Chandela (Vijayapala) and the Somavamshi Yayati without decisive result, took Varanasi (Pala-ruled until at least 1016) and Prayaga, and saw Ahmad Niyaltigin raid Varanasi in 1033, plundering it until noon before…

wars.name: Lakshmikarna's eastern campaigns
wars.outcome: The 1048-49 Rewa inscription claims successes in Anga and Vanga; the invasion of Gauda "was repulsed by Nayapala"; no land held; peace later sealed by the marriage of Yuvanashri to the Pala king.

wars.name: Fall of Bhoja and the war for Malwa
wars.outcome: Lakshmikarna and Bhima of Gujarat attacked Malwa about 1055 and Bhoja fell; Jayasimha regained the throne in 1055 with help from Vikramaditya VI; Lakshmikarna and Someshvara II took Malwa again until Udayaditya drove them out about 1073.

wars.name: Kalachuri-Chandela wars
wars.outcome: Vijayapala "broke the pride of Gangeyadeva in a battle"; Lakshmikarna subjugated Devavarman and was ousted by Kirttivarman before 1075-76; Madanavarman "captured the northern part of Baghelkhand" from Gayakarna.

wars.name: Ratnapura independence
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II declared independence; Gayakarna's army "was defeated".

certainty.note: No treaty line on any page opened; Dahala (Baghelkhand and the Jabalpur country) is the stable core, every other limit is approximate.
